frontier.hypothesis: The site-swap (E-s22-3) plus E-s22-1's condition (ii) names one untried chassis: loop 1's exit tail is a FRESH READ (target's lw) into a SECOND carried name `r`, and `r` is used ONLY as loop 2's base addend, so that `r` dies exactly at loop 2's preheader copy. Every chassis measured so far keeps a single carried name `p` that is still live into the post-loop-2 re-reads, so a copy of it would not have a dying source and optimize_reg_copy_1 would not re-point the base add.
frontier.mechanism: E-s22-1: target's order needs (i) a copy insn before the base add and (ii) REG_DEAD on the copy's SOURCE at that copy. Splitting the carried pointer into two names makes (ii) satisfiable for loop 2 for the first time, while the loop-1 exit re-read supplies target's lw at the site where we currently emit a move.
frontier.next_probe: Build on V1: keep loop 1 exactly as-is except the tail, which becomes `r = *(u8 **)(ctx + 0xC);` (a fresh read, defined on both paths - also insert the same read on the skip path by hoisting it above loop 1's guard ONLY if the skip path needs it, and measure both spellings). Loop 2's guard reads `r`; loop 2's preheader writes an explicit C copy `s = r;` with `base = (u8 *)(sh2 + (s32)s);` and NO further use of `r` anywhere after (the post-loop math args, rec_a and rec_b keep their own re-reads, so `r` dies at the copy). Then, before scoring, run pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 and check the ONE diagnostic from E-s22-2: does .cse's loop-2 preheader contain (set (reg X) (reg Y)) with Y the addend? Score with sandbox --disable all and record build_insns.

frontier.hypothesis: The s16 trichotomy's 'in-block use -> combine deletes the copy' branch has never been read in a dump, only inferred behaviourally. If the deletion is done by flow rather than combine, or if the copy survives to .lreg in some spelling, the branch is not closed and s17's abstract can_combine_p enumeration may have priced the wrong pass.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c substitutes and deletes a copy whose single use it can fold; flow.c deletes copies whose destination is dead. The two have different escape hatches, and s17 enumerated only the former.
frontier.next_probe: Take V1 and build the minimal in-block-use cell (loop 1's `q` used only by the base add, i.e. delete the `p = q;` tail), dump with pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1, and locate the copy insn number in .cse, then check its presence in .combine and .flow. Record which dump first lacks it. That single fact decides whether s17's can_combine_p ladder is the right ladder.

frontier.hypothesis: Because target's two loop preheaders are byte-identical to each other apart from body offsets, the original C almost certainly used the SAME construct twice; the reason our second copy dies may be that our second construct is written differently from our first rather than that the site is structurally poorer.
frontier.mechanism: E-s22-3 established loop 1's construct (redundant ctx+0xC read folded by cse into a copy, destination used past the join) reproduces target byte-for-byte including hard registers. Symmetry says the same shape must be reachable at loop 2 with a use past loop 2's join.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the sites past loop 2's exit that are NOT reload-deleters (E-s21-3 killed math-args, rec_a, rec_b, and the end-pointer derivation - nine cells across two chassis). The one class never tried: a use on the SHARED return-0 path or in the *(s16 *)(ctx + 0x6) increment chain that mentions the pointer without replacing any existing ctx+0xC read. Build one such cell only if a semantically honest spelling exists; otherwise record the enumeration as complete and close the axis.
